title: VF-023's third probe: does the model java.util.List re-declaring Collection's methods fix JBMC's dispatch of size() on a choice of two lists
description: Values stream of llm-dlc/loops/application-core.md (llm-dlc/loops/application-core-values.md, acceptance row V2; finding VF-023 in verification/findings.md), at the commit that submits this job. The second probe (job 20261108-091002-..., passed) found that JBMC 6.11.0 refutes l.size() whenever l is a choice between two lists made on different branches (two List12s included) and proves it for one list alone; its trace of oneOrTwo(n=1) shows JBMC calling ImmutableCollections$ListN.size on a List12, which returns 0. Each refuted probe also reaches java.util.List.size() as JBMC's stub: the model java.util.List (lib/models/java/util/List.java) declares List's own abstract methods but not the ones it inherits from Collection (size, isEmpty, iterator, ...), and Collection is not on JBMC's class path, whereas the JDK's List re-declares them. This job changes nothing in the repository and fixes nothing (no timebox attempt). verification/triage/vf023-dispatch.sh runs six property proofs with JBMC alone (jvmcontract prove --engine jbmc, default unwind 16, timeout 300 s each) in two class-path variants: as-is (the tool's models) and declared (the models' java.util sources with Collection's 15 abstract methods re-declared in List, compiled with javac --release 8 into lib/target and passed with --classpath, which precedes the tool's models on JBMC's class path). Probes: the corpus's listSizes [assume n >= 1 && n <= 3; assert result == n * 10] and listChange [assume n == 0 || n == 8; assert result == 1], oneOrTwo, oneOrThree, emptyOrOne and oneAssumed. For each it records the verdict and, from jbmc-goto.txt, the probe method's dispatch of size()/isEmpty() (the class-identifier tests and the functions called). Domain: one int n under each probe's assumption. Expected: as-is reproduces the second probe (oneAssumed proved, the five others not verified: JBMC's counterexample does not reproduce); declared is the hypothesis under test, all six proved if it holds. Process status: exit 0 either way (the script reports, it doesn't judge). If declared proves all six, the next step is that change in lib/models with values::LIST_MODEL bumped, checked by resubmitting job 20261108-070211-...'s corpus steps, as VF-023's last timebox attempt.
expected: exits 0; summary.txt names each variant's six verdicts and the dispatch of size() in each probe method; as-is: oneAssumed proved, the other five not verified; declared: the hypothesis holds if all six are proved

resources.notes: twelve JBMC runs over methods of a few lines: the second probe's nine took 5.8 s in all
